A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FCGS research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression, rendering-quality, runtime, and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds component measurements, split-count ablations, and reduced-training-data experiments.

M1.justification: The architecture, MEM paths, context models, loss structure, and coding sequence remain intact. Equation 7 locally revises the stated entropy-probability computation from Gaussian density evaluations to quantization-bin CDF differences. This establishes a change in the mathematical specification, without establishing that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DL3DV-GS, MipNeRF360, Tank&Temples, Deep Blending, MVSplat outputs on ACID, and LGM outputs on Gobjaverse. The new 100-scene training experiment changes the data budget within existing coverage, not the dataset or task.

E2.justification: The quantitative benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Figure 5 adds Simon and SOG to the qualitative comparison; appendix Figure E adds Simon, Navaneet, Light, and SOG to the examples previously comparing FCGS with 3DGS. HAC and ContextGS receive discussion, not new evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and training settings are retained. New controlled experiments vary inter-Gaussian batches from 2 to 5, intra-Gaussian chunks across 2/4/8/16, and training-set size from 6670 to 100 scenes. Component timing additionally specifies single-GPU measurement.

E4.justification: Appendices G-J and L substantially expand the diagnostic evaluation with storage and codec-time breakdowns, split-count sensitivity, bit-allocation visualization, and reduced-data training. Appendix B adds a quantified MVSplat mask failure. Existing MEM, context, hyperprior, sampling, and pruning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the same five-seed Gaussian-splitting analysis, reporting a storage standard deviation of 8e-4 MB and coefficient of variation of 3.6e-5. v3 introduces no additional repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and MEM/context/hyperprior scores remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table N reports 30.981 MB and 29.256 dB after training on 100 scenes, versus 27.440 MB and 29.264 dB with 6670 scenes. Other additions include decoding times, component bit costs, split-count results, qualitative baseline scores, and an approximately 0.7 dB MVSplat penalty from inferred masks.

T1.justification: Equation 7 replaces the Gaussian-density expression with weighted Gaussian CDF differences across quantization intervals, correcting the formal treatment of discrete coding probabilities. Equation 3 also explicitly specifies sigmoid thresholding. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: generalizable optimization-free FCGS compression, MEM and contextual entropy modeling, compression exceeding 20x with preserved fidelity, and compatibility with pruning methods. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 expands the existing domain-gap limitation with a concrete MEM misrouting explanation and explicitly acknowledges inferior compression performance to HAC and ContextGS, explaining the anchor-based representation difference. New appendices interpret component costs, diminishing benefits from additional splits, latent bit allocation, and reduced-data robustness, substantially broadening the scientific discussion.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies four-layer analysis/synthesis MLPs, three-layer hyperprior transforms, the 0.01 mask threshold, a zero context placeholder for the first batch, and model storage below 10 MB. These are additional disclosures; the existing hardware, training pipeline, and code-access destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds CodecNeRF to related work and the references. It also develops the distinction from the already-cited ContextGS in Section 3.3 and discusses positioning relative to HAC and ContextGS in Appendix D. The broader research framing remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged. Local explanations and captions are revised, corresponding-author information and acknowledgements are added, and the appendix is reorganized: former E.1-E.3 become F, M, and K, while Appendix B is retitled and expanded.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to expose MEM routing. Figure 5 and the appendix qualitative grid gain baseline columns, with the latter rotated to accommodate the expansion. Seven new tables and a bit-allocation heatmap substantially extend the displays. Tables C-E explicitly annotate the existing initial 3DGS training costs.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already extensively evaluated method through targeted sensitivity tests, decoding and component-cost measurements, qualitative baseline comparisons, clearer limitations, and more reproducible specifications. The discrete-likelihood correction improves mathematical precision. These provide useful additional support without changing the central benchmark evidence. A new sentence in Appendix G reverses the lambda-storage trend shown in its tables, but this limited error does not outweigh the gains.
